verdict.line: You lose if you trade freely before level 6 into his Q stacks and W stun; you win if you survive to your R and outscale with core items.

brief.thesis: K'Sante owns the trade patterns before level 6 through Q (Ntofo Strikes) poke and the W (Path Maker) stun, which is why lane and solo-kill advantage sit with him. Mordekaiser's 51.7% win rate over 860 games comes from surviving that window with W (Indestructible) sustain and then flipping the fight once R (Realm of Death) and core items come online.

theirWindow.when: He is about to hit 2 Q stacks
theirWindow.what: Back out of the short line his Q travels in — the 2nd stack fires a shockwave that pulls you in, and his passive marks whatever it lands on for bonus damage on his next attack.

yourWindow.when: His W (Path Maker) is on cooldown (14-10s)
yourWindow.what: Step in and trade with Q (Obliterate) plus autos — without the charge-up stun he has no way to lock you down, and every hit you land builds toward your passive's damage aura and move speed.

powerCurve.note: neither side has real trade tools yet
Q stacks plus W stun punish extended trades
your R and his All Out both come online
Rylai's and Riftmaker turn trades one-sided
full build wins any drawn-out fight

start.why: The mana from Ring keeps you spamming Q/E through his poke phase, and the potions cover the early trades you lose before you have Indestructible's shield stacked up.

boots.why: K'Sante's damage is physical-heavy through auto-attacks empowered by his passive marks — flat physical reduction blunts that far more than Mercury's Treads' tenacity does in this matchup.

core.why: The slow from Q and E makes it much harder for him to walk away once you commit Death's Grasp, and it's the first piece in the highest win-rate path (68.8% over 48 games).
Omnivamp stacks with W's stored-damage heal to win extended trades once he's out of his early stun window.
Burn damage punishes him for standing in Death's Grasp range or tanking your Q, and it closes out the 68.8%-winrate build path.

situational.when: he builds into lifesteal or heal-reliant items to out-sustain your damage
you need the grievous wounds earlier than Thornmail's power spike
his team stacks hard CC on top of his W stun
the game goes long and you need more raw defensive stats to keep tanking

runes.keystoneWhy: The stacking adaptive force rewards the same extended trades Indestructible is built to win, and it's the keystone behind both measured rune pages.

summoners.why: Ignite (55.2% win rate, 70.2% pick) offsets the shield he generates from E (Footwork) and the healing from his All Out, denying the sustain that lets him win extended fights.

playing.title: Never fight into 2 Q stacks
playing.detail: Step out of his short-line Q before he reaches the second stack — that stack fires a shockwave that pulls you in, and his passive marks you for extra damage on the follow-up attack.

playing.title: Trade the moment his W is down
playing.detail: W (Path Maker) is his only stun and it's on a 14-10s cooldown with a visible charge-up — punish immediately after he uses or whiffs it, since he has no other way to lock you in place.

playing.title: Bank your shield before all-ins
playing.detail: Don't consume Indestructible's shield for the heal the instant it's up — hold it through his damage spike so you're converting his hits into your sustain, not wasting it early.

playing.title: Land three hits to trigger Darkness Rise
playing.detail: Chain Q, an auto, and E in the same trade so your passive procs mid-fight — the damage aura and move speed swing extended trades hard in your favor.

playing.title: Time R around his All Out
playing.detail: Realm of Death shares a similar power spike with his R (All Out, 120-80s cooldown) — use it to isolate and steal his stats before he gets to go All Out on you, not after.

playing.title: Play the wave, not the poke, before level 6
playing.detail: Lane and solo-kill advantage sit with him pre-6, so shove and reset rather than absorb free Q poke — you have nothing to punish his stun with until your ultimate is up.

brief.patchCaveat: Build order, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample numbers are pulled from measured games on the current patch (16.19.1); the mechanical read on cooldowns, tells, and trade timing is our own analysis.
